newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank intervening to support crown-dealer.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank intervening to support crown-dealer.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB), for the second consecutive day, is intervening on the crown market to support the ailing currency, a dealer said.
A dealer at BNP-Dresdner in Prague told Reuters several deals had been confirmed, while dealers at bank CSOB said the CNB was checking rates but could not confirm any deals had been struck.
"We have concluded a deal with the central bank, I can tell you that," the BNP-Dresdner dealer said.
A dealer at another bank said the CNB was looking to deal, and that while his bank had not struck any deals, he believed others had.
"We saw some requests from the CNB. I believe they dealt some tens of millions of marks on the market," the dealer said.

The crown opened the day at about 3.8 percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket midpoint, but lost ground to around -3.95 percent despite a 50 basis point rise in the central bank's repo rate to 12.9 percent.
At 0820 GMT, the crown was trading at 3.69 percent on the depreciation side of basket parity.
"The repo rate rise was already built into the market, so its effect is minimal," one dealer said.
Late on Thursday the CNB said it had decided to raise its repo rate, but had not set a target for how much it would rise, instead allowing "market conditions" to be the determining factor.
Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka said he had not struck any deals with the central bank, but that he too believed some had been struck at other banks, and that volumes were increasing slightly.
"The volumes are tens of millions of dollars so far, the individual deals are under tens of millions," he said.
"They (the CNB) will try to keep it (the crown) under four percent, but so far it's been a fifty-fifty fight, I would say," Becvar added.

Thursday's rate announcement came after the crown plunged to a record low of five percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity, prompting the CNB to intervene on the market to support the currency for the first time in over a year.
